title: Adding delivery zones to a large orders table
name: Orders delivery zone migration

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these migrations add and populate the new column on a large, busy table? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The deploy is interrupted halfway through the index build in the first migration, and it is re-run. What happens?
choices: The migration fails because the column already exists
The whole migration runs in a transaction and was rolled back, so it starts cleanly
The add_column is skipped via if_not_exists, and the index creation is retried; a leftover invalid index from the interrupted build is not dropped automatically by this code
The index is recreated twice, producing duplicates

questions.prompt: Why does the backfill define MigrationOrder inside the migration instead of using the application's Order model?
choices: To avoid loading the database schema
To keep the migration independent of later changes to the Order model, such as new callbacks, validations or renamed associations that would run or break on old migrations
Because Order cannot be queried with in_batches
To bypass the table's foreign keys

questions.prompt: While the backfill is running, new orders keep being created. How is the NOT NULL rule reached safely?
choices: The constraint is added NOT VALID, so only new and updated rows are checked immediately and existing rows are checked later, during the separate validation step
The constraint is validated first, so any new NULL row would be rejected during the backfill
The column is changed to NOT NULL in the backfill migration itself, which rewrites the table
The model's before_validation callback makes the database constraint unnecessary
